reader.summary: This week in Switzerland was dominated by the UBS capital crisis, as CEO Sergio Ermotti made his clearest threat yet to relocate the bank out of Switzerland over regulatory capital demands. The government confirmed it had assessed the impact of a UBS exit, the lower house committee is set to debate the issue in November, and employee groups warned of major job losses. A top Geneva banker called a departure 'bad news' for the city. In health, Switzerland confirmed the arrival of a Swiss woman evacuated from Nigeria after contracting Ebola, with 52 contacts placed under surveillance in Geneva. The evacuation put Nigeria's healthcare system in the spotlight and prompted Ghana to tighten prevention measures. In sports media, Swiss TV's commentary on Israel's Olympic bobsleigh team was ruled discriminatory by the national regulatory authority, with complaints formally upheld. Diplomatically, the Swiss foreign minister made a rare visit to North Korea to discuss security and political ties, while China and Switzerland celebrated a new trade deal that bucks global protectionist trends and opens access for Swiss firms in the drug and finance sectors. In sports, three-time Grand Slam champion Stan Wawrinka retired with a defeat at the Swiss Indoors in Basel. The Swiss supreme court also upheld a landmark 20-year war crimes sentence for a Liberian ex-rebel commander. The central bank posted a $23 billion profit driven by gold and foreign assets.

display.eli5:
Switzerland is in the middle of a big fight about its biggest bank, UBS. The CEO has threatened to move the bank out of the country if the government keeps demanding more capital. Next week, parliament will start debating the issue, and that is where the real action will be.

This matters because UBS is one of the world's largest banks, and if it leaves Switzerland, thousands of jobs in Geneva and other cities could disappear. The government says it has already looked at what an exit would mean, and now politicians have to decide whether to bend the rules or risk losing the bank.

Meanwhile, the Ebola case that had everyone worried will wind down. The Swiss woman who was evacuated from Nigeria is in a Geneva hospital, and the people she was in contact with are being monitored. Once that monitoring period ends, the story will mostly be over.

A surprise would be if a big Swiss pharma or banking company suddenly announces it is investing heavily in China under the new trade deal. That would show the agreement is really working and not just a handshake photo.

In a separate health scare, Swiss authorities confirmed that an Ebola patient in Nigeria was the wife of a Swiss diplomat, who had reportedly contracted the virus in Uganda rather than in the Democratic Republic of Congo. On the economic front, UBS won a legal victory against former Credit Suisse managing directors over back-pay claims, while Swiss watch exports posted a fifth consecutive monthly rise driven by demand in the US and Europe.
